description: Result pattern for ASP.NET Core (.NET 10+). Services return Result<T>, Result or Error; one call at the endpoint turns it into a typed success response or an RFC 9457 ProblemDetails error. Minimal API first, MVC supported, NativeAOT-safe. Packages: ResultCrafter.Core, ResultCrafter.AspNetCore, ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.EfCore, ResultCrafter.FluentValidation, ResultCrafter.AspNetCore.FluentValidation.
rules: Register once in Program.cs: builder.Services.AddResultCrafter() and app.UseResultCrafter().

Services return Result<T>, Result or Error. Endpoints map them with ToOkResult(), ToCreatedResult(), ToAcceptedResult(), ToNoContentResult() or ToProblemResult(). Never return a Result, Result<T> or Error from an endpoint without mapping it.

Create results only through the factories (Result<T>.Ok, Created, Accepted; Result.NoContent, Accepted; Error.NotFound, Conflict, BadRequest and the rest) or the implicit conversions. Never use default(Result<T>) or default(Result).
The To*Result method must match how the result was created: a Created result needs ToCreatedResult(). A mismatch throws InvalidOperationException.

Declare error responses for OpenAPI with .ProducesNotFound(), .ProducesBadRequest() and the other Produces* extensions on Minimal API endpoints, or the [ProducesNotFound] style attributes on controllers.
Error.With(key, value) and FieldError.With(key, value) accept only string, int, long, bool, double, decimal, Guid, DateTimeOffset, DateTime or string[] values.

For field errors a client should translate, return Error.BadRequest(new Dictionary<string, FieldError[]> { ["email"] = [new FieldError(message, code)] }). The body keeps errors and adds errorCodes with the same keys. Never put the value the caller sent into FieldError args.
